purpose: REGF2 version of grid B: the same network, operating points and events, with the REGF2 unit (VSM) in the slot. Selection grid: the same machines re-arranged (one 7-8 tie circuit out, a new load at the device's HV bus, different dispatch and voltage schedule). Held-out runs only; the solver never sees it, and its score is the one the RSI accept rule uses.

case.name: grid_B2
case.description: Kundur two-area re-arranged: device in GENROU 3's slot; one of the three 7-8 tie circuits (Line_6) out of service; a new 200 MW load PQ_3 at the device's HV bus 9; 150 MW load PQ_2 at bus 10; loads moved from bus 8 to bus 7; device at 720 MW (above any training dispatch) with a 1.02 pu voltage schedule; device REGF2

device_under_test.params_note: ANDES inputs. The six REGF1 parameters drawn the way REGF1's were (ANDES defaults scaled by numpy default_rng(seed).uniform(0.7, 1.3, 6) in the order wdrp, Qdrp, Tpm, KPplim, KIplim, Tr; wdrp and Qdrp times Sb/Sn), with seed 1 instead of REGF1's seed 0, so the two units do not share numbers; KPv = 6 as for REGF1; mf = 27, so Tint = mf*wdrp = 0.0997 s (ANDES's default 0.15 gives under 1 ms with the base-corrected wdrp, which is REGF1's law). dd and the auto-added PLL2 keep ANDES's defaults (dd = 0.11, Kp = Ki = 0.1). The same device sits in grids A2, B2 and M2.

design_notes: Grid B with REGF2 instead of REGF1 (Nov 10), so the two devices are compared on identical grids and a harness that alternates between them sees the same networks. Grid M's dispatch and schedule were chosen for REGF1's damping (see grid_M.json); they have not been re-checked for REGF2 with an EIG scan.

The device's loading decides whether a voltage-loop error is visible at all. At 550 MW a 30% error in the voltage-loop gain KPv cost 0.02 to 0.06 on a line trip, at 700 MW 0.16 to 0.22, and at grid A's op1 it saturates. 720 MW keeps that error visible without saturating and sits just above the training dispatch.
